units.title: hw2
examples: ocean facts: deepest point, km per degree of latitude and longitude, what sets the speed of sound, the sound channel
why the sky is blue; wave speed, wavelength and frequency; which colour travels farthest in water
width of the equatorial Pacific in degrees and km; why a great-circle flight heads north

units.title: hw3
examples: describe temperature and salinity with depth from Atlantic sections
potential temperature of air aloft and water at depth; read sigma-t from a T–S diagram
practical salinity from the conductivity ratio (polynomial)
why cold fresh water can float on 4 °C water, and whether that happens in the sea
units.notes: 4 question record(s): OCW-2.011-HW3-P2, OCW-2.011-HW3-P3, OCW-2.011-HW3-P4, OCW-2.011-HW3-P5

units.title: hw4
examples: frequency or wavelength of sound in air and water

units.title: hw7
examples: Coriolis deflection of a thrown ball in each hemisphere and at the equator
sketch Ekman transport, sea-surface slope and geostrophic flow round Antarctica

units.title: exams
examples: describe a circumpolar current; model a passage as a channel for its velocity profile and transport
